column4: what exactly, and where the evidence is

*** Asked on 15 September 2026 whether outstanding work was tracked centrally, this archive checked and the answer was no. *** Errands for David were well kept in data/errands.tsv; *** what was NOT tracked anywhere was the archive's OWN next actions ***, which lived scattered across per-topic TSVs and page prose. *** The cost was real: an errand telling David to go and find the 1791 marriage act sat at status 'ready' for hours after the act had been found and published. *** This file is the single list. *** data/errands.tsv = work for a person. THIS FILE = work for a session. data/gaps.tsv = what cannot be closed at all. ***

column1: *** THE BERROETA CONTROL - run this before anything else ***
column4: *** Search FamilySearch full text for a phrase known to be in the regiment's book *** - *** 'Capellan del Regimiento Infanteria de Buenos Ayres', or the chaplain's name BERROETA ***. *** It decides a day of work. *** If it returns hits from the castrense collection, that book is indexed, and the absence of Llerena from the 68 'Sancho Llerena' results becomes a real finding won in one search. If it returns nothing, the book is not indexed and images 663-950 must be read by hand. *** Error 15 blocked it on 15 September; the block lifts in about an hour. NO ZERO FROM A BLOCKED PAGE WAS RECORDED AS A NULL. *** See data/castrense-1791-walk.tsv.

*** DGS 7713373. Images 652-662 are read (Dec 1787 - Jul 1791, no Llerena). 663 to about 950 are NOT, and they run to 1814. *** About 290 images, a day's work rather than an hour's. *** Do the Berroeta control first - it may make this unnecessary. ***

column1: *** TWO FULL-TEXT COLLECTIONS FOUND AND NEVER OPENED ***
column4: *** Montevideo, Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepcion - Baptism Records 1825-1828 ***; and *** Nuestra Senora del Carmen, Cordon - Religious Marriage Records 1825-1916 ***. Both surfaced in the 'Sancho Llerena' full-text sweep of 15 September 2026 and neither has been looked at. *** The Cordon marriage register in particular spans the generation this archive is weakest on. ***

column1: *** THE 68 RESULTS WERE NOT FULLY HARVESTED ***
column4: *** Only about fifty titles and THREE snippets were actually read before Error 15 returned. *** The remaining results have not been examined, and results 51-68 were never displayed. *** Re-run 'Sancho Llerena' at 100 results per page and extract every ark, then resolve each through the tile service's manifest.json to a film and image - that route works even while www is blocked. ***

column1: *** DGS 7713375 - a film with two known acts and nothing else read ***
column4: *** Montevideo Cathedral baptisms. The 1789 godparent act is image 551; the 1811 baptism of Luis is image 2410. *** Identified on 15 September 2026 and never systematically read. *** It spans at least 1785-1811, which is the whole of Sancho's Montevideo life. ***

column1: *** THE SANCHEZ QUESTION - it cuts against this archive's own argument ***
column4: *** Is the 'Manuel Sanchez, Sargento de dicho Regimiento' of the castrense book (30 January 1791, DGS 7713373 image 660) the same man as the 'Juan Manuel Sanchez, natural del Reino de Andalucia' of the Canelones informaciones (March 1791, DGS 8166573 images 1462-1464)? *** If yes, a soldier of that regiment DID leave an informacion at the Canelones vicaria, and *** the suggestion that military jurisdiction explains Sancho's absence from that series collapses. *** The castrense entry's birthplace runs off the page edge - *** re-read image 660 at the right-hand margin first. ***

column1: *** THE INFORMACIONES: ONE CAVEAT NOT YET CHASED ***
column4: *** The filming card at DGS 8166573 image 1461 reads 'HOJAS SUELTAS' - loose leaves. *** The volume's order is whatever order somebody filed them in. *** A stray January 1791 sheet could sit anywhere in Volumen 7, images 1460-1827, and the walk only established that it is not where it should be. ***

*** DGS 7713386 is NOT it *** - images 300 and 1500 are cathedral burial registers of 1887 and 1905. *** The index may still exist under another DGS. *** Find it the way the Canelones one was found: an image's Information tab prints the catalogue link and that reel's item-by-item contents. See data/castrense-1791-walk.tsv and the correction of 15 September 2026.

*** 'Cordova la Llana' is the CITY of Cordoba, Andalusia *** - settled 15 September 2026. So Sancho was born there about 1767 and *** his parents Felix Llerena and Rosalia Aguilar were natives of the same city. *** *** Nobody has yet looked for a single Cordoba parish register. *** That is now the largest unopened door in the archive, and it is in Spain rather than Uruguay.

column1: *** ANTON ARMANDO LERENA - a live contradiction, not merged ***
column4: *** gendatabase.com says born 1952, died 2003. The archive's existing row from ancestors.co.za says died 2013 aged 68, implying born about 1945. *** Those cannot both describe one man. *** They may simply be two men, and they have deliberately NOT been merged. *** See data/gendatabase-sa.tsv.

*** Five of the fifteen gendatabase death rows carry 1999: Catherine Tertia Karon, Gayle Lerena, Pierre Frederick Lerena, and two children aged eight and thirteen. *** *** Either something terrible happened to this family in 1999 or the index has a default-year artefact, and a summary row cannot say which. *** Settle it from the death notices themselves before any of it is published as fact.

*** The 1994 death notice of RICARDO JUAN CARLOS LERENA (b.1920, m.1941 Doreen May Chappell), from gendatabase.com. *** A South African death notice *** names the deceased's PARENTS *** - which would put in a modern official document what this archive currently infers: that the Cape Lerenas descend from Pablo Armando. Already logged in data/errands.tsv.

column1: *** AND THE STANDING RULE THIS SESSION KEPT BREAKING ***
column4: *** Names in eighteenth-century hands CANNOT be read at fit-width. *** On 15 September 2026 this archive misread, in one sitting, *** a chaplain as 'Mendoza' when he is BERROETA, a slave-owner as 'LLERENA' when he is Francisco Juarez, and a mother as 'Rosalia Illera' when she is Petrona Illescas. *** *** The second of those would have manufactured a Llerena inside the regiment's own book - the exact thing the archive wants to find. *** None reached the site. *** Magnify before believing, and magnify hardest when the reading is the one you were hoping for. ***
